items.title: Step 1
items.description: Begin your project by adding an `img` element with a `src` of `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-1.png` within the `body` element.

hints.text: Your code should have an `img` element.
The `img` element should have a `src` of `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-1.png`.

items.title: Step 2
items.description: In previous lessons about the CSS box model, you learned that every HTML element is treated as a box with four areas. Imagine you receive a box from your favorite online retailer — the content is the item in the box, or in your case, a header, paragraph, or image element. Change the `src` attribute in the `` from `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-1.png` to `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-2.png`.

hints.text: The `img` element should have a `src` of `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-2.png`

items.title: Step 3
items.description:
The content is surrounded by a space called padding, similar to how bubble wrap separates an item from the box around it.

Think of the border like the cardboard box your item was shipped in.

Change the `src` attribute to `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-3.png`

hints.text: The `img` element should have a `src` of `https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/curriculum/css-box-model/diagram-3.png`

items.title: Step 4
items.description:
Margin is the area outside of the box, and can be used to control the space between other boxes or elements.

Here the bottom element has a larger top margin, pushing it further down the page.

Now that you quickly reviewed the CSS box model, it's time to get started on the Rothko painting.

Remove the `img` element.

hints.text: You should not have an `img` element in your code.

items.title: Step 5
items.description:
Add a `div` element in the `body`.

Set the `class` attribute equal to `canvas`.

This will act as the canvas for your painting.

hints.text: Your code should have a `div` element.
The `div` element should have a `class` with the value `canvas`.

items.title: Step 6
items.description:
Before you can start styling the `div` you added, you need to link your CSS to your HTML.

Add a `link` element to link your `styles.css` file. Set the `href` to `styles.css`, and remember to set the `rel` attribute to `stylesheet`.

hints.text: Your code should have a `link` element.
Your `link` element should have a `rel` attribute with the value `stylesheet`.
Your `link` element should have an `href` attribute with the value `styles.css`.

items.title: Step 7

hints.text: Your code should have a `.canvas` selector.
You should set the `width` property to `500px`.
Your `.canvas` element should have a `width` of `500px`.

items.title: Step 8
items.description: Add the `height` property with the value `600px` to your `.canvas` rule.

hints.text: You should set the `height` property to `600px`.
Your `.canvas` element should have a `height` of `600px`.

items.title: Step 9
items.description: Change the `background-color` of the canvas to `#4d0f00`.

hints.text: You should set the `background-color` property to `#4d0f00`.
Your `.canvas` element should have a `background-color` of `#4d0f00`.

items.title: Step 10
items.description:
Every painting needs a frame.

Wrap the `.canvas` element in another `div`. Give that `div` the `frame` class.

hints.text: You should add a new `div` element.
Your `.canvas` element should be nested in the new `div` element.
Your new `div` should have a `class` with the value `frame`.
Your new `div` should be within your `body` element.

items.title: Step 11
items.description:
Write a new rule using the `.frame` class selector.

Use the `border` shorthand declaration to give the `.frame` element a solid, black border with a width of `50px`.

hints.text: Your code should have a `.frame` selector.
You should set the `border` property to `50px solid black`.
hints.test:
const hasBorder = new __helpers.CSSHelp(document).getCSSRules().some(x => x.style.border === '50px solid black');
assert(hasBorder);

hints.text: Your `.frame` element should have a `border` property with a value of `50px solid black`.
hints.test:
const frameBorder = new __helpers.CSSHelp(document).getStyle('.frame')?.getPropertyValue('border');
assert(frameBorder === '50px solid black');

items.title: Step 12
items.description:
The frame is much too wide.

In `.frame`, set its `width` to 500 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `width` property to `500px`.
Your `.frame` element should have a `width` of `500px`.

items.title: Step 13
items.description:
Use padding to adjust the spacing within an element.

In `.frame`, use the `padding` shorthand property to increase the space between the `.frame` and `.canvas` elements by `50px`. The shorthand will increase space in the top, bottom, left, and right of the element's border and canvas within.

hints.text: You should set the `padding` property to `50px`.
Your `.frame` element should have a `padding` value of `50px`.

items.title: Step 14
items.description:
Use margins to adjust the spacing outside of an element.

Using the `margin` property, give the `.frame` element vertical margin of `20px`, and horizontal margin of `auto`. This will move the frame down 20 pixels and horizontally center it on the page.

hints.text: You should set the `margin` property to `20px auto`.
hints.test:
const hasMargin = new __helpers.CSSHelp(document).getCSSRules().some(x => x.style.margin === '20px auto');
assert(hasMargin);

hints.text: Your `.frame` element should have a `margin` value of `20px auto`.

items.title: Step 15
items.description:
Add a new `div` element inside of your `.canvas` element.

Give the new `div` the `class` attribute with a value of `one`. This will be your first rectangle.

hints.text: You should create a new `div` element.
You should nest the new `div` element within your `.canvas` element.
Your new `div` should have a `class` attribute with a value `one`.

items.title: Step 16
items.description: Write a new rule that targets `.one` and set its `width` to 425 pixels.

hints.text: You should have a `.one` selector.
You should set the `width` property to `425px`.
Your `.one` element should have a `width` value of `425px`.

items.title: Step 17
items.description: Now set the `height` for `.one` to 150 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `height` property to `150px`.
Your `.one` element should have a `height` value of `150px`.

items.title: Step 18
items.description: Set the `background-color` of `.one` to `#efb762`.

hints.text: You should set the `background-color` property to `#efb762`.
Your `.one` element should have a `background-color` value of `#efb762`.

items.title: Step 19
items.description:
Use margins to position the `.one` element on the canvas.

Add the shorthand `margin` property with a vertical margin of `20px` and a horizontal margin of `auto`.

hints.text: You should set the `margin` property to `20px auto`.
hints.test:
const marginFilter = new __helpers.CSSHelp(document).getCSSRules().filter(x => x.style.margin === '20px auto');
assert(marginFilter.length === 2);

hints.text: Your `.one` element should have a `margin` value of `20px auto`.

items.title: Step 20
items.description:
Now `.one` is centered horizontally, but its top margin is pushing past the canvas and onto the frame's border, shifting the entire canvas down 20 pixels.

Add `padding` of `1px` to the `.canvas` element to give the `.one` element something solid to push off of.

hints.text: You should set the `padding` property to `1px`.
Your `.canvas` element should have a `padding` value of `1px`.

items.title: Step 21
items.description:
Adding 1 pixel of padding to the top, bottom, left, and right of the canvas changed its dimensions to 502 pixels x 602 pixels.

Replace the `padding` property with `overflow` set to `hidden` - changing the canvas back to its original dimensions.

hints.text: You should remove the `padding` property from the `.canvas` selector.
You should set the `overflow` property to `hidden`.
Your `.canvas` element should have an `overflow` value of `hidden`.

items.title: Step 22
items.description: Add another `div` with a `class` value of `two` just below your `one` element. This will be your second rectangle.

hints.text: You should not change the existing `.one` element.
You should have a second `div` element in your `.canvas` element.
Your second `div` element should have a `class` value of `two`.
Your `.two` element should come after your `.one` element.

items.title: Step 23
items.description: Create a new CSS rule using the `.two` selector and set its `width` to 475 pixels.

hints.text: You should have a `.two` selector.
You should set the `width` property to `475px`.
Your `.two` element should have a `width` value of `475px`.

items.title: Step 24
items.description: Set the `height` of the `.two` element to 200 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `height` property to `200px`.
Your `.two` element should have a `height` value of `200px`.

items.title: Step 25
items.description: Set the `background-color` of the `.two` element to `#8f0401`.

hints.text: You should set the `background-color` property to `#8f0401`.
Your `.two` element should have a `background-color` value of `#8f0401`.

items.title: Step 26
items.description: Center the `.two` element by setting its `margin` to `auto`.

hints.text: You should set the `margin` property to `auto`.
Your `.two` element should have a `margin` value of `auto`.

items.title: Step 27
items.description: Create a new `div` with a `class` value of `three` right under the `.two` element. This will be your third rectangle.

hints.text: Your existing `.one` and `.two` elements should not be changed.
Your new `div` should be nested in your `.canvas` element.
Your new `div` should come after your `.two` element.
Your new `div` element should have a `class` with the value `three`.

items.title: Step 28
items.description:
You don't always have to use pixels when sizing an element.

Create a new rule, `.three`, and set its `width` to `91%`.

hints.text: You should use the `.three` selector.
You should set the `width` property to `91%`.
Your `.three` element should have a `width` value of `91%`.

items.title: Step 29
items.description: Set the `height` of `.three` to `28%`.

hints.text: You should set the `height` property to `28%`.
Your `.three` element should have a `height` value of `28%`.

items.title: Step 30
items.description: Change the `background-color` of `.three` to `#b20403`.

hints.text: You should set the `background-color` property to `#b20403`.
Your `.three` element should have a `background-color` value of `#b20403`.

items.title: Step 31
items.description: Center the `.three` element on the canvas by setting its `margin` to `auto`.

hints.text: You should set the `margin` property to `auto`.
Your `.three` element should have a `margin` value of `auto`.

items.title: Step 32
items.description:
It's helpful to have your margins push in one direction.

In this case, the bottom margin of the `.one` element pushes `.two` down 20 pixels.

In the `.two` selector, use `margin` shorthand property to set top margin to `0`, horizontal margin to `auto`, and bottom margin to `20px`. This will remove its top margin, horizontally center it, and set its bottom margin to 20 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `margin` property to `0 auto 20px`.
hints.test:
const hasMargin = new __helpers.CSSHelp(document).getCSSRules().some(x => x.style.margin === '0px auto 20px');
assert(hasMargin);

hints.text: Your `.two` element should have a `margin` value of `0 auto 20px`.

items.title: Step 33

hints.text: You should set the `filter` property to `blur(2px)`.
Your `.canvas` element should have a `filter` value of `blur(2px)`.

items.title: Step 34
items.description: Create a rule that targets both `.one` and `.two` and increase their `blur` effect by 1 pixel.

hints.text: You should have a `.one, .two` selector list.
You should set the `filter` property to `blur(1px)`.
Your `.one` element should have a `filter` value of `blur(1px)`.
Your `.two` element should have a `filter` value of `blur(1px)`.

items.title: Step 35
items.description: Increase the `blur` of `.three` by 2 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `filter` property to `blur(2px)`.
Your `.three` element should have a `filter` value of `blur(2px)`.

items.title: Step 36
items.description:
The rectangles are too small and their edges don't have the soft quality of a painting.

Increase the area and soften the edges of `.one` by setting its `box-shadow` to `0 0 3px 3px #efb762`.

hints.text: You should set the `box-shadow` property to `0 0 3px 3px #efb762`.
Your `.one` element should have a `box-shadow` value of `0 0 3px 3px #efb762`.

items.title: Step 37
items.description: Use the same `box-shadow` declaration for `.two`, but change the color from `#efb762` to `#8f0401`.

hints.text: You should set the `box-shadow` property to `0 0 3px 3px #8f0401`.
Your `.two` element should have a `box-shadow` value of `0 0 3px 3px #8f0401`.

items.title: Step 38
items.description: Add a `box-shadow` to `.three` with the values `0 0 5px 5px #b20403`.

hints.text: You should set the `box-shadow` property to `0 0 5px 5px #b20403`.
Your `.three` element should have a `box-shadow` value of `0 0 5px 5px #b20403`.

items.title: Step 39
items.description:
The corners of each rectangle are still too sharp.

Round each corner of the `.one` element by 9 pixels, using the `border-radius` property.

hints.text: You should set the `border-radius` property to `9px`.
Your `.one` element should have a `border-radius` value of `9px`.

items.title: Step 40
items.description: Use the `border-radius` property on the `.two` selector, to set its top-left radius and bottom-right radius to `8px`, and top-right radius and bottom-left radius to `10px`.

hints.text: You should set the `border-radius` property to `8px 10px`.
Your `.two` element should have a `border-radius` value of `8px 10px`.

items.title: Step 41
items.description:
The `border-radius` property accepts up to four values to round the top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left corners.

Round the top-left corner of `.three` by 30 pixels, the top-right by 25 pixels, the bottom-right by 60 pixels, and bottom-left by 12 pixels.

hints.text: You should set the `border-radius` property to `30px 25px 60px 12px`.
Your `.three` element should have a `border-radius` value of `30px 25px 60px 12px`.

items.title: Step 42
items.description:
Rotate each rectangle to give them more of an imperfect, hand-painted look.

Use the `transform` property on the `.one` selector to `rotate` it counterclockwise by 0.6 degrees.

hints.text: You should set the `transform` property to `rotate(-0.6deg)`.
Your `.one` element should have a `transform` value of `rotate(-0.6deg)`.

items.title: Step 43
items.description: Rotate the `.two` element clockwise by 0.4 degrees.

hints.text: You should set the `transform` property to `rotate(0.4deg)`.
Your `.two` element should have a `transform` value of `rotate(0.4deg)`.

items.title: Step 44
items.description:
Rotate `.three` counterclockwise by 0.2 degrees.

With this final step, your Rothko painting is now complete.

hints.text: You should set the `transform` property to `rotate(-0.2deg)`.
Your `.three` element should have a `transform` value of `rotate(-0.2deg)`.
